narrative.overview: The site should feel like the seat the shop saves for you: warm, unhurried, and a little worn-in. Cream paper carries the reading, espresso brown carries the weight, and caramel is the small glint of something freshly poured. Everything is soft: pill buttons, rounded cards, a serif with gentle personality.
keyCharacteristics: Five-color brown-and-cream palette; no cool neutrals, no pure black or white.
Serif display (Fraunces) over a neutral sans (Inter) for all functional text.
Pill-shaped actions, 16px cards, hairline latte borders.
Flat, tonal depth; shadow only as a response or on the single hero medallion.
Alternating cream and latte bands, with espresso reserved for the hero, quotes, and footer.

rules.name: The Warm Only Rule
rules.body: Every neutral is tinted brown. Never introduce gray, pure black (#000), or pure white as a solid; the white card fill is always translucent (60%) over cream.

rules.name: The Glint Rule
rules.body: Caramel marks a small thing worth noticing (a price, a label, a number). It is not a section background and not body text; keep it to large or bold text and verify AA before using it for small copy.

rules.name: The Serif Speaks Rule
rules.body: Only headings and testimonial quotes use Fraunces. Prices, nav, buttons, and hours are always Inter.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. Shadows appear on hover, or on the hero medallion, and nowhere else.

dos: Do build from the five palette colors; use espresso for text, mocha for secondary text, caramel as the accent.
Do keep action shapes pill-round and containers 16px.
Do alternate cream and latte/50 bands between sections.
Do keep eyebrows uppercase, tracked at 0.1em, and caramel.
Do keep prices, hours, and address as plain Inter text a phone can read at a glance.
donts: Don't use pure black, pure white, or any gray.
Don't put Fraunces on prices, buttons, nav, or form-like data.
Don't add resting shadows to cards or buttons.
Don't use caramel for small body text on cream without checking AA contrast.
Don't add dark borders or square corners.
Don't treat emoji as final art; they are placeholders for real imagery.
